subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add an agent-controlled pre-compaction lifecycle contract, and may that contract include bounded agent-requested deferral across the compaction boundary?
rationale: The implementation gap is clear, but handoff and DEFER semantics add public config, workspace-write timing, checkpoint semantics, and possible approval carryover that require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Adopt warnings and checkpointed handoff first
options.body: Add opt-in threshold warnings plus a structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

options.title: Adopt full bounded deferral
options.body: Allow ALLOW/BLOCK/DEFER semantics only with explicit max duration, audit trail, idempotent checkpoint matching, workspace scope, and approval-expiry rules.

options.title: Decline new lifecycle surface
options.body: Keep memoryFlush, notifyUser, hooks, and checkpoint APIs as the supported compaction surfaces and document recovery patterns instead.

recommendation.title: Adopt warnings and checkpointed handoff first
recommendation.body: Add opt-in threshold warnings plus a structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal for the current pre-compaction memoryFlush path, and the remaining question is product/security scope for extending that lifecycle.
